title: Allow DDS files to be imported as streamed textures.

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
The PR makes it so you can import DDS files as streamed textures.

DDS files have had a bit of a mixed history.  A previous commit adds dds files to the image loader, which resulted in dds textures being imported via the regular texture path which meant texture data could be re-compressed resulting in unwanted artifacts from double lossy compression.  That was eventually reverted.

DDS files are not currently imported resources.  There is a resource loader which loads them directly into a texture so there are no import options at all.  Since they are not imported, they get exported as is and you have no way to change that.

To use them as streamed textures the current approach presents some problems.  First, selecting the streamed texture type is an import option.  Second, normally an imported resource is copied into the import folder and only the imported copy gets exported with the game.

To solve these problems this PR takes the following approach.  A resource importer is added for dds files.  This importer is the default for dds files (to match existing behavior).  Rather than copy the dds file into the import folder, a small reference file is written instead, which just points to the real file.  To make this work, the exporter is taught that some files are exported as is.  This approach was taken to preserve compatibility as much as possible.  The original DDS file is at its original location at it default imports as a DDS texture as it does today.

In addition to the above, a second resource importer is added to import to a streamed texture.  These do get copied to the import folder in the streamed texture format, in which case, the original DDS file is not exported.

In both cases, you will now get a .import file for DDS files where you didn't before since they are now an imported resource instead of a directly loaded resource.  I don't think there is a way around this without more hacky solutions.  I tried lots of different attempts from export plugins, customized exports.  Lots of them somewhat worked but this seemed the cleanest approach in the end.
